headings.text: Expose your product to the UI correctly
Pick a unique port and slug

blocks.html:
This is the durable checklist for any product integration API, independent of stack. It distils the patterns in the template and the Matrix/MediaMTX examples. For org-wide tooling, CI, and style rules, see Community & Standards (in Contribute to Project), which links pvarki/markdown-pvarki-best_practises and pvarki/config-ci-library.

Implement the required callbacks

Your service must answer all five lifecycle endpoints under /api/v1/users/ (created, revoked, promoted, demoted, updated). The template generates them as NotImplementedError stubs.

  • Implement the events your product needs; acknowledge the rest with return OperationResultResponse(success=True) — never leave a stub raising NotImplementedError, or the core rmapi's user operations will fail.
  • Return success=False only on a real failure; the core rmapi treats it as a failed operation.
  • Make handlers idempotent — the same callback may be retried. Look up by alias/uid and skip if already done (as Matrix does with rooms).

Trust only the core rmapi

Guard every callback (and any per-user endpoint like clientinfo/proxy) with mTLS and the CN pin:

def comes_from_rm(request: Request) -> None:
    payload = request.state.mtlsdn
    manifest = get_manifest()
    if payload.get("CN") != manifest["rasenmaeher"]["certcn"]:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403)

• Read trust material from the deployment manifest (/pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json), not hard-coded values.
  • Trust the deployment CA the platform provides — do not bundle your own CA or skip verification. On Docker Compose certs come via kw_product_init and the ca_public volume; on Kubernetes the CA arrives as the opendefense-bundle ConfigMap/Secret synced by trust-manager. (See the stack-specific Register your integration pages.)

Expose your product to the UI correctly

Serve GET /api/v2/description/{language} returning a ProductDescriptionExtended with a ProductComponent of the right type:

  • **link** — point ref at a real external URL (not https://example.com).
  • **markdown** — serve per-user Markdown at POST /api/v2/clients/{language}/info.md; the core rmapi proxies it at /api/v1/product/proxy/<short_name>/....
  • **component** — build the ui/ bundle to dist/; it is served at /ui/<short_name>/remoteEntry.js. Keep the clientinfo payload (ClientInfoData) in sync with the UI's expected type.

Provide real fi and sv translations, not just en (missing languages fall back to en).

Health check honestly

GET /api/v1/healthcheck ships returning healthy=True unconditionally. Make it check the services your API actually depends on and report healthy=False (with details in extra=) when they are down — orchestration and readiness probes rely on it.

Pick a unique port and slug

  • The internal app_port must be unique on the shared product network.
  • On Docker Compose, product integration APIs are reached on the conventional Product integration APIs port **4626** via nginx; the service binds its own internal port.
  • Use one consistent short_name everywhere — package name, subdomain, UI slug, manifest key.

Versioning

Use bump-my-version: bump-my-version bump <patch/minor/major>. The scheme combines a semantic version with an autoincrementing calendar build (e.g. 1.0.2-260420); always bump the semantic part, never build on its own. Preview with bump-my-version show-bump.

Don'ts

  • Don't call your service rmapi — that name belongs to the core RASENMAEHER API. Name yours <short_name>rmapi.
  • Don't accept unauthenticated lifecycle calls or trust any CN other than the rmaeher cert CN.
  • Don't block startup on slow dependencies — bootstrap in a background task and queue/defer work (the Matrix deferred queue is the pattern).
  • Don't invent endpoints the core rmapi doesn't call; keep to the documented contract and add product-specific endpoints behind the same mTLS guard.
  • Don't hard-code domains, ports, or CA paths — read them from the manifest and the platform-provided trust bundle.
